summary.one_liner: Google's free Technical Writing One course teaches clearer technical documentation through active voice, paragraph structure, terminology, audience awareness, and basic Markdown.
takeaways: Write in active voice and convert passive sentences to active voice.
Structure paragraphs around a single topic with clear lead sentences, and state key points at the start of documents.
Identify your target audience and the curse of knowledge, and decide what they already know and need to learn.
Use terminology, acronyms, and punctuation (commas, colons, em dashes, semicolons) consistently, and reach beginner Markdown competency.
summary.summary: This is the introduction page for Google's Technical Writing One course, a self-paced course on the fundamentals of technical writing focused on clarity, conciseness, and audience awareness. It lists learning objectives such as recognizing ambiguous pronouns, converting passive to active voice, shortening sentences, building lists, and organizing sections. The course has a pre-class part that works standalone and an in-class part that adds to it, and it needs an internet connection with optional short videos and optional units. The page states that the course improves writing but does not turn you into a great technical writer on its own.
